contexts.text: Thus he could never be saved to eternity, which is to live to eternity ().
If they had been instructed in the mysteries of faith, they would have perished to eternity. Signified, Explained.
To live to eternity is... to live after death in eternal damnation.
The days of eternity (; ) = the Most Ancient Church. AC 477:3. AC 1259:6. AC 2906:6. AC 6075:2. AC 6239:3. AC 6280:end. AC 8159:2.
Would he wish to destroy his soul to eternity?
Hence it may be evident, that the Earth will not last to eternity...
Such could not but be kept in some Hell to eternity...
The quality of a man... is at once known by the Lord from eternity, and what he will be to eternity.
Under Covenant, see this reference. AC 2054. AC 2084.
Their situation is constant, nor is it varied to eternity.
The profanation of what is holy is attended with eternal damnation. AC 2520:end.

Men cannot apprehend eternity except as an eternity of time... The very idea itself of the Divine eternity (is insinuated into the Angels) by this, that thousands of years do not appear to them as time, and scarcely otherwise than as if they had lived a minute; and (also) by this, that in their present they have past and future things together: hence they have no solicitude about future things; nor at any time any idea of death, but only an idea of life. Thus in all their present there is the eternal and the infinite of the Lord.
That which a man derives from the father remains to eternity.

The things which are discordant with the eternal life, that is, with the spiritual and celestial life, which is the eternal life, if not removed in the life of the body, are removed in the other life; and if they cannot be removed, the man can never be otherwise than unhappy to eternity.
The hereditary evil from the father is interior, and remains to eternity...
Evil Spirits would not desist to eternity...
Otherwise (mankind) would have perished by the death of the damned to eternity.
By this Internal, man lives... to eternity.
For an eternal possession () = what is eternal.
He willed (thus) to save mankind to eternity.
If goods and evils were commingled, man would perish to eternity. AC 2284:2. AC 2426:end.
Thus they would not live to eternity.

The life is more heavenly in proportion as it is far from the things of space and time, and is near to the things which are eternal; in which, namely, in what is eternal, there is nothing whatever from the idea of time, nor from what is analogous to it.
All eternity is present to Him.
Thought and view from the Divine extend to each and all things which shall take place to eternity.
This with ineffable variety to eternity.
Year, and years... = eternity, when they are predicated of the Lord's Kingdom in Heaven. Illustrated.
The Lord alone sees the state of man; not only the present state, but also what it will be to eternity. AC 6214:end.
Man would then perish to eternity; for, in the other life, he would hang between Hell and Heaven...
The origin of light was from eternity, from the Lord alone... The Divine Human, which was from eternity (), was that Light itself.
This state (of progress) is continued, with those who are in good, after the life of the body to eternity.
The danger of eternal condemnation, if Divine truth and Divine good be profaned. Signified.

The Divine is infinite as to being, and eternal as to manifesting; and that which is finite cannot comprehend the... eternal, for the eternal is the infinite as to manifesting... Wherefore, the things which are infinite and eternal are presented before the Angels in appearances, which are finite; but still in such things as are very far above the sphere of man's comprehension; as, for example, man can never have any idea of eternity except from time; and because of this incapability, he cannot comprehend what from eternity is, thus what the Divine was before time or before the world was created; and so long as there is in his thought anything of idea from time, if he thinks about from eternity, he must necessarily fall into errors from which he cannot be extricated; but to the Angels, who are not in the idea of time, but in the idea of state, it is given to perceive this perfectly well; for eternity with them is not an eternity of time, but an eternity of state without the idea of time. AC 8325:2.
For in the Lord everything is infinite and eternal; infinite relatively to being, and eternal to manifesting.
(Consequences going on to eternity. See Consequence.)
As the Lord has foreseen from eternity what a man would be, and what he will be to eternity, it is evident that Providence is present in the smallest things...
See Bless.
The being of man is nothing but a recipient of the eternal which proceeds from the Lord... The reception of life is that of which manifesting is predicated.
The happiness of eternal life is what, in the supreme sense, Eternity corresponds to, which Eternity is from the Divine being of the Lord.

In the supreme sense, yesterday = from eternity; today = eternity; and tomorrow = to eternity; for the times mentioned in the Word = states... and with the Lord there are no states, but everything there is eternal and infinite.
Evil of guilt, or the evil which man has contracted through actual life, and has also confirmed in thought, even to faith and persuasion, cannot be amended, but remains to eternity.
He had been the Light itself from eternity...
He is continually being conceived and born... in the other life to eternity. AC 5122:3. AC 5202:4. AC 5354:3. AC 8326:end.
Each and all things are foreseen by the Lord, what their quality will be to eternity.
If the internals (of Hamor and Shechem) had been closed up, they would have perished to eternity.
Eternal rejection. Signified. Under an oak = to eternity. Explained.
The things which are thus conjoined can never be separated to eternity, wherefore the deepest Hell awaits them.
Asher, in the supreme sense, = Eternity; in the internal sense, the happiness of eternal life.
For the things which are once confirmed in both doctrine and life at the same time, remain to eternity. Explained.
Therefore it is said of the Lord that He is the Last and the First... and by this, in the relative sense, is signified what is perpetual; and in the supreme sense, what is eternal.
To build according to the days of Eternity () = according to the state of the Church in ancient times.
This Divine, or this Jehovah in Heaven, is the Lord from eternity.
Universal nature... is a representation of the eternal and the infinite; of the eternal from propagation even to eternity...

Providence, being from the Divine, has in it the eternal and the infinite; the eternal, because it regards neither a terminus from which nor a terminus to which... That in each and all things which the Lord does there is what is infinite and what is eternal, will be illustrated by examples elsewhere. AC 5503.
To foresee is to Know from eternity to eternity.
Man is such evil, that to eternity he cannot be fully delivered, even from one sin...
It is this Man that the Lord... united to the Divine Itself, as He had been united from eternity; for from eternity He was one.
The Angels are being perfected to eternity...

Eternity is predicated of the Most Ancient Church, because it was in the good of love to the Lord, of which good eternity is predicated because it is immediately from the Lord. The generations of Eternities () = the goods thence.
Eternity is predicated of Judah (), because by Judah is represented the Celestial Church.
Eternity () is predicated of the good of love; for justice is said of it.
Unless eternity () were predicated of what is celestial; and generation, of what is spiritual... it would be a useless repetition.
This is the Divine Human from eternity. (See Divine Human.)
The mountains of Eternity () = the good of love which was of the Most Ancient Church... When this Church is understood in the Word, being the most ancient one, there is sometimes added Eternity.
That the Providence of the Lord... regards what is eternal. Example(s). AC 8478:4. AC 8560. AC 10775:end.
According to order from eternity. Signified.
In the other life (the growth of good and truth) is immense, and this perpetually to eternity.
In the Word, it is said to eternity, and to generation of generations ... because eternity is predicated of Divine good; and generation of generations, of Divine truth.
Not from eternity. Signified.

In the Divine... instead of time, there is eternity. Infinity and eternity are the two things to which correspond the times and spaces which are in the world; and the states as to being and as to manifesting which are in the Heavens.
From now, or from today = eternity, thus to eternity, because it involves the time following.

The Lord's life there to eternity. Signified. (For) everything which is given as an inheritance, is the perpetual possession of him to whom it is given, in Heaven the eternal one, because they live there to eternity.

When they are elevated into Heaven, they are afterwards perfected to eternity. But they who are cast into Hell... endure evils which are continually worse, until they dare not do evil to any one; and they afterwards remain in Hell to eternity...
To keep this word even to eternity () = that all this must be observed hereafter.
Ye shall see them again no more for ever = that the falsities which are once removed shall be removed to eternity.
Jehovah shall reign for ever and to Eternity () = that the Lord alone is the God of Heaven and earth. Explained.
The conjunction of good and truth to eternity. Signified.
(It is necessary to learn from revelation) that man will live to eternity; if he has lived well, in Heaven; and if evilly, in Hell.
God sees all things, and knows all things from eternity; and provides all things to eternity.
Not considering, that the Divine blessing consists in being happy to eternity, and that the Lord regards momentary things... no otherwise than as means to eternal ones...
And also believe in thee to eternity () = that there may be the faith of truth which shall be permanent.
There is no proportion between what is temporary and what is eternal... The infinite as to time is the eternal.

He shall serve him perpetually = to eternity... It is said to eternity, because they who do what is good from the obedience of faith, and not from the affection of charity... in the other life can never be brought to a state of good... Wherefore... they remain such to eternity.
The regeneration of man in the world is only a plane for the perfecting of his life to eternity. AC 9452.
The life in the world remains with everyone to eternity.
For he who once conquers the Hells, conquers them to eternity.
For everything which the Lord ordains, that is, provides, with man and Angel, is eternal.
An age = what is eternal.
What is eternal in the Spiritual Kingdom. Signified.
Generations = what is eternal. Explained, Illustrated.
Eternity is predicated of the Divine Celestial or good; and generation, of the Divine Spiritual or truth.
Overagainst its faces = to eternity. (For) that which is overagainst the faces there, is in the Lord's perpetual view, thus is preserved to eternity.

The infinite relatively to duration is the eternal. Hence it is that whatever the Lord disposes and ordains is eternal... There are in man external, internal, and inmost things; and all these are disposed and ordained simultaneously and successively to the reception of things that follow, to eternity.
In your generations = to eternity with those who are in faith from love.

Unless the Natural is purified and cleansed with man while he lives in the world, it cannot be purified afterwards to eternity; for such as the Natural of man is when he dies, such it remains. Explained.
It shall be to them the statute of an age = an eternal law of order...
See Age.
Man is such, and remains such to eternity, as is his love.
Many in that (Third) Earth believe that their spirits have existed from eternity...

The goods, happinesses, and felicities which are... provided for man by the Divine, are eternal ones, and have no end... The temporary to the eternal, as the finite of time to its infinite, has no proportion. That which lasts to eternity Is, but that which has an end relatively Is not... AC 10409:4.
This was the Lord from eternity. Explained.
To be conjoined with God is to live to eternity.
Hence such as a man's love and such as his faith has been when he lived in the world, such does his life remain to eternity...
Keeping goodness to thousands = to eternity... To thousands = in perpetuity and to eternity. References.
Hence it is evident, that those who come into Hell remain there to eternity; and that those who come into Heaven remain there to eternity.
(It is from possessing this Inmost) that man lives to eternity.

As the Angels have not any notion of time, they have a different idea of eternity from that of men of the Earth. By eternity the Angels perceive infinite state, and not infinite time. I was once thinking about eternity, and through the idea of time I could perceive what to eternity is, that it is what is without end; but I could not perceive what from eternity is, thus neither what God was doing before creation from eternity. On this causing me anxiety, I was elevated into the sphere of Heaven, and thus into the perception in which the Angels are concerning eternity, and then I was enlightened that eternity is not to be thought of from time, but from state, and that then what from eternity is is perceived; which, also, took place with me. TCR 31:3. CL 328:3.
His dominant affection or love remains with every man after death; it is not extirpated to eternity. Explained.
They who are in Heaven are continually advancing to the springtime of life... and this to eternity...
I saw that the extent of the uninhabited Heaven is so great, that it cannot be filled to eternity...
Through this, the Rational (of Spirits and Angels) is continually being cultivated, and this to eternity.

With every Spirit and Angel there remains the affection, as to both magnitude and quality, which he had in the world; and this is afterwards perfected through infilling, which also takes place to eternity; for there is nothing which cannot be infilled to eternity; for every thing can be infinitely varied...
There is a reigning love which remains with man after death, nor is it ever changed to eternity.
That man after death remains to eternity such as he is as to his will or reigning love. General article.
Hence it is, that man remains to eternity as his life of love has been in the world.
Wherefore, such as a man is as to his interiors, such he remains to eternity.
That the Divine Human from eternity was the Divine truth in Heaven... References.
That this was the Son of God born from eternity. References.
That every Divine work regards what is infinite and eternal. General article.
That every man after the life in the world lives to eternity. General article.

The spiritual man, when separated from the natural, remains such as he is to eternity; for the state of man cannot be changed after death. Moreover, the Spiritual of every man is in conjunction with the Divine... and that which can be thus conjoined with the Divine, to eternity cannot die; for the Divine is with him, and conjoins him with itself.
(How it is that the evil also live to eternity.) Explained.
Their lot after death, although it is to remain to eternity, they account of slight value.
That the Lord from eternity is Jehovah. General article. Illustrated.
Death (the rider on the pale horse) = eternal damnation.
He thus keeps Hell... in obedience to Him to eternity.
In every Divine work there is a union of love and wisdom; from this comes its perpetuity, nay, its Eternity.

He who... cannot from some perception think of God apart from time, is quite unable to perceive eternity otherwise than as an eternity of time; and then he cannot but rave in thought concerning God from eternity... From this idea he cannot be extricated, except by the spiritual or angelic idea about eternity, which is apart from time; and when it is apart from time, the eternal and the Divine are the same. The Divine is the Divine in itself, and not from itself. The Angels say that they can indeed perceive God from eternity, but in no wise nature from eternity... Being in itself is life itself, which is the Divine love of the Divine wisdom, and the Divine wisdom of the Divine love. This is eternity to the Angels; thus abstracted from time...

The creation of the universe... cannot be said to have taken place... from time to time, thus progressively and successively; but from eternity and infinity; not from an eternity of time, because there is no such thing, but from an eternity not of time, for this is the same as the Divine... TCR 31:3.

When it is said that... (an eternity of time is not possible, everyone affirms it from reason), because this is an infinity of time. If one say, to eternity, this is comprehended from time; but not so, from eternity, unless time is removed.
In these two faculties the Lord is with every man... Hence it is that every man, both good and evil, lives to eternity.
That in all the forms of uses there is some image of what is infinite and what is eternal. General article. DP 56.
By drawing nearer, this conjunction (of man with the Lord) may be augmented to eternity; and with the Angels it actually is augmented to eternity...
That in all it does the Divine Providence regards what is infinite and what is eternal. General article. DP 55.
That the Infinite in itself, and the Eternal in itself, is the same as the Divine. General article.
By what is eternal the Angels understand the Divine manifesting.
There cannot be an infinity of time which is eternity a quo, because what is infinite is without first and last, that is, without boundaries.

From thought abstracted from time and space, there is a comprehension... of the Divine from eternity; but none at all from thought in which there inheres an idea from space and time. (Thus) it is possible to think about God from eternity, but never about nature from eternity.
That the Infinite and the Eternal in itself cannot but regard what is infinite and eternal from itself in finite things. General article.

As they who are in the Divine think from the Lord, they think from what is eternal while they think from what is present; saying to themselves, What is that which is not eternal? Is not what is temporary comparatively as nothing?... It is otherwise with what is eternal; this alone Is, because its being never comes to an end. To think in this way is to think from what is eternal at the same time as one is thinking from what is present; and when a man so thinks and at the same time so lives, the Divine proceeding with him... in all its progression, regards the state of his eternal life in Heaven, and leads to that. In every man, both evil and good, the Divine regards what is eternal.
That an image of the Infinite and the Eternal stands forth in the angelic Heaven. General article.
That to regard the Infinite and the Eternal in forming the angelic Heaven... is the inmost of the Divine Providence. General article.

The adult who does not come into freedom itself and rationality itself in the world, can never come into them after death; for then the state of his life remains to eternity such as it had been in the world.
That the Divine Providence regards eternal things, and temporary things no otherwise than in proportion as they agree with eternal things. General article.
By eternal things are meant those which do not perish and cease with time, thus not with life in the world.
That eternal things relate to spiritual honours and wealth, which are those of love and wisdom, in Heaven. General article.
That when dignities and wealth are blessings, they are spiritual and eternal...
That temporary and eternal things are separated by man, but that they are conjoined by the Lord. General article.
What temporary things are, and what eternal things. Explained.
That man is in himself temporary, and that the Lord is in Himself eternal; and that therefore from man there can proceed only what is temporary, and from the Lord only what is eternal.
That temporary things separate from themselves eternal things; and that eternal things conjoin with themselves temporary ones.
That the conjunction of temporary and eternal things with man is the Divine Providence of the Lord. General article. DP 220:8.
That it is of the Divine Providence that by death man puts off... temporary things, and puts on... eternal things.
That through His Divine Providence the Lord conjoins Himself... with temporary things through eternal things according to uses.
That everything confirmed in the will and at the same time by the understanding endures to eternity; but not that which is only confirmed by the understanding.

With the good these spirals turn forwards, but with the evil backwards... and as when the turning is once induced it cannot be reversed, it is evident, that such as a man is when he dies such he remains to eternity...
That every man is created to live to eternity.
He who can receive the Divine, so as to see and perceive it in himself, cannot be otherwise than conjoined with the Lord, and, through this conjunction, live to eternity.
In Heaven they remain to eternity (in the age of early manhood).
All the present is to Him eternal.

The operation of the Divine Providence is said to last to eternity, because every Angel is perfected in wisdom to eternity; but everyone according to the degree of the affection of good and truth in which he was when he left the world: it is this degree which is perfected to eternity...
As this goes on to eternity, there is no last or ultimate which is the close.
At last they find a Society which perfectly agrees with their affections, and there they dwell to eternity.
They thus become mere falsities as to the understanding, and so remain to eternity.

They shall be tormented day and night for ages of ages = that they... were cast into Hell, where they will be interiorly infested by the love of their falsity and by the lusts of their evil constantly to eternity.
For such as a man is in the world as to the spirit, such he remains to eternity; with the sole difference, that his state becomes more perfect if he has lived well...
(I said), By the birth of the Son of God from eternity, I understand His birth foreseen from eternity and provided in time.
The delight of the love of uses eternizes these delights.
He perceives his happinesses ascending in a like degree (with marriage love); and these constant to eternity.
The reigning love... remains with the man to eternity, and together with it the subordinate loves.
The appearance that love and wisdom... are in man as his, causes man... to be able to be conjoined with God, and thus live to eternity.
How can man live to eternity, unless he is conjoined with an eternal God?
Thus be conjoined with the Lord, and thereby become man, and live to eternity.
That with those who are in love truly conjugial, this conjunction becomes more and more inward to eternity.
Because eternity is the infinite of time.
That those who are in love truly conjugial, in marriage regard eternity...
(The effect on two married partners in Heaven from whom the idea of eternity in relation to marriage was taken away.)

(I said), You can think of the essence and omnipresence of God from eternity, that is, of God before the creation of the world, because you think of the essence of God from eternity apart from time, and of His omnipresence apart from space...
I can therefore testify for certain, that everyone is there explored... and that the life which he has contracted in the world remains with him to eternity...
That the infinity of God... relatively to times is called Eternity... but still there is nothing of time in His Eternity. General article.
The reason the infinity of God relatively to times is called Eternity, is that to eternity is predicated of things progressive, which are measured by time, without end. Example(s).

In Heaven... by Eternity, the Angels perceive the Divinity as to manifesting; also... by Eternity they perceive the Divinity as to wisdom: the reason is that from the Divinity the Angels abstract... times; and then these notions result. But as man cannot think otherwise than from ideas taken from such things as are of space and time, he cannot perceive anything... of His Eternity before times; nay, when he wants to do so, it is as if his mind fell into a swoon...
There appear two statues... at one extremity of the Spiritual World, by which those who think vain things about God from eternity seem to themselves to be swallowed...
Eternity, etc., pertain to the Divine being.
They asked those who were in that prison, whether they would live so to eternity. Some there replied, We have been here some ages, and we shall remain for ages of ages...
The celestial sense of the (first) commandment is, that Jehovah the Lord is infinite, immense, and eternal...
As the spiritual life has no end, it is eternal; wherefore being can be predicated of it.
Reciprocal conjunction with God causes... that after death man lives to eternity...
With every man of sound mind, there is the faculty of receiving wisdom from the Lord... to eternity; and also of receiving love... to eternity.

The only thing they then think about is Eternity... I wanted to know from them how their thought could be fixed on Eternity alone, unless at the same time on eternal life. But they said that they could not then meditate on anything but eternity, and that it involved the same as eternal life. They tried to induce... the state of their Society on my... mind...

As man supposes... that the soul of man will be tormented to eternity, this is evident, - that man is condemned to eternal suffering; for he has deserved it; but of the Lord's mercy damnation is at last taken away...
What is eternal was represented as an abyss without a bottom...
Punishments... do not alter or change the nature, which remains to eternity as contracted in the life of the body...
There was one who supposed... that infernal punishments would last to eternity...
It has been decreed from eternity...
What are forty or fifty years... to Eternity?

Certain corporeal Spirits... could not perceive time from eternity; for that there is an eternity to come they could perceive from the fact that there is no end to time; thus that it is time without end; but that there has been time from eternity they cannot conceive...

(I said) that no words are applicable to the Lord except eternal and infinite; and that only the eternal and infinite Is... And, as nothing but eternal things can be predicated of Him, the past, the present, and the future are all eternal. They wondered that the present should be called eternal, but as (the above) is the case, although no idea of it can possibly be perceived, it follows that our present is to Him eternal.

On what is eternal. As the infinite Divine is not of space, so neither is the eternal of time... That a kind of idea of the Divine eternal is insinuated into the Angels by the Lord, is evident from the fact... that they have no idea of past and future things, but that both past and future things are in their present... Neither is there in their idea anything of old age or of death, but only of life; wherefore there is none of time; but in all their present there is as what is eternal.
On those who think that there is an origin to all things, thus that God is not eternal.

They who are in the idea of time cannot think otherwise than by means of time, that eternity is nothing but time; when yet with the Lord each and all things are eternal, and the idea of time cannot agree with the idea of eternity.
By this idea it was impressed, that whether nature is eternal... or the Lord, the anxiety begins to be set at rest.

(Thus) while man lives in the world, he acquires for himself a fixed plane, and this cannot be changed; whence it is, that man remains to eternity such as he has become in the world. He has this plane in him, but it is completely quiescent: but still his interiors cease in it.
I then clearly perceived that he who once comes into Hell remains there to eternity...
Unless what is eternal is thought of, that is, an eternal conjunction, there is no wife, but a concubine; and from the idea of what is not eternal, marriage love perishes.
On the quality of the idea of... the eternal from the idea... of time.
The smallest movements of man's life have a series of consequences to eternity... Hence it may be evident, that the eternal of the Lord... is from the Lord...

From Him who is the all in all of Heaven and the Church, from eternity to eternity. Signified. For all times in the Word = states of life... Therefore, when the Lord is treated of, they = infinite state; and infinite state, as to time, is eternity... Many things might be said concerning eternity, which is of the Lord alone; but they would not be understood by the natural man, whose thoughts are chiefly founded on time, space, and matter, when yet eternity does not include such things in it; and therefore if a man could think about eternity as the Angels do, he might come into some idea of it, and thus comprehend what from eternity is... also what the Divine foresight is, that it is in every single thing from eternity; and what the Divine Providence is, that it is in every single thing to eternity; and therefore that whatever proceeds from the Lord is from eternity to eternity; and that unless this were the case, Heaven and the universe would not subsist.

Eternal cannot be expressed in Heaven by any other word than Divine. The reason is, that what is infinite cannot fall into an angelic idea, and still less into a human one, and the eternal is the infinite manifesting from the infinite being; but this falls only into the idea that the eternal, which is the Divine as to manifesting, is the all in all of Heaven and the Church...
Such as is the determination of the interiors of a man's mind, such does he remain after death to eternity...
For man remains to eternity such as he is (at the end of his life in the world); namely, such as his life has been to that period.
After death, man remains to eternity in that state of life which he has acquired in the world; wherefore, he must watch.

All things which are in the spirit of man remain with him to eternity... Those things remain in the spirit of a man which he has thought from himself, consequently, those things which he has thought from his own love when he was alone...

Thou shalt not know in what hour I will come upon thee = ... thou art ignorant of the state of life that will remain to eternity; for such as is the state of a man's past life up to its end, such does the man remain to eternity. Illustrated.
(Note) that man remains to eternity such as he is as to his whole life up to the end, and not at all such as he is at the hour of death...
He shall no longer go out = that they shall be therein to eternity.
The reason for ever and ever = what is eternal, is that in the world these words = times as to all their duration; but in Heaven... they = what is eternal.

The removal of evils and thence of falsities at the end of life and afterwards to eternity. Signified. For he who fights against evils and falsities, and conquers them in the world up to the end of life, conquers them to eternity; for such as a man, from his past life, is at the end of life, such he remains to eternity.
Eternal damnation. Signified.

Hell, here, = eternal damnation, because they who once come into Hell, remain there to eternity; wherefore, also, it is said and Hell followed with him; for to follow with him = to remain in it; namely, in damnation to eternity.
It is natural to say for ages of ages, but spiritual to say to eternity.
The mountains of Eternity () = the Celestial Church, and love to the Lord.
Lest there be a representative of eternal damnation. Signified.
The seed of the malicious shall not be mentioned to eternity () = eternal dissociation and separation.
Even to eternity will I make firm thy seed () = the Eternity of the Divine truth from Him. To eternity will I keep mercy for him () = the Eternity of the Divine good from Him.
Hence it was evident, that such as a man is when he dies, such he remains to eternity.
The eternal is the Divine as to manifesting.

This being is meant by the eternal; for the eternal, when predicated of the Lord, is understood in Heaven without any idea of time... For, in the angelic idea, the eternal is the state of the Divine manifestation... The infinite manifesting, which, also, is the eternal, is the Divine proceeding.
It shall not be inhabited to eternity () = its destruction to eternity...
Hence it is, that such as a man is in the world, such he remains to eternity...
As God is uncreate, He is also eternal. Explained.
The natural idea of eternity is from time; but the spiritual idea of it is not from time.
The Inmost... through which man lives to eternity.
They fall into Hell; nor can they be taken out to eternity.
They were asked whether they were able to think of His having been born from eternity...

The reason the Lord says, that He was with the Father as they are from eternity, is that in the world He was the Divine truth, which is the Divine proceeding; whence it is evident what is the Son of God from eternity, and the Son of God that was born. No mortal can comprehend what born from eternity means in any other sense. Ath 149.
7. This is why Spirits and Angels can subsist and live to eternity. Explained.
4. 2. In this is the eternal; and where there is the eternal there is also the infinite.
God 3. 6. 7. 9. This very God is from eternity; and thence is Eternity itself.

comment.comment: #problem Shouldn't the ref immediately below be simply 'God 3.'? The 6. 7. 9. all follow later.

contexts.text: God 3. 5. The infinity of God correspondently to times is called Eternity.
God 3. 6. Still, there is nothing of time in His Eternity.
God 3. 7. By the Eternity of God is meant His Divinity as to manifesting.
God 3. 9. Angels and men... cannot comprehend His immensity and Eternity, as they are in themselves.
52. This truly Christian Church... will last to eternity...
